name: Labra
subtitle: a soft mixed vegetable torkari fragrant with panch phoron and ginger

ingredients.note: the sweetness that holds labra together
for a gluten-free dish use compounded-free hing — most brands are cut with wheat flour

prepNotes: Cut everything to roughly 3cm so the hard and soft vegetables finish at the same time.
Toast 1 tsp of the panch phoron in a dry pan and crush it — this goes in at the end as a finishing powder.
Labra wants to be stirred with a light hand; use a wide kadhai so you can fold rather than mash.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil to smoking in a wide kadhai, then reduce the heat.
Add the bay leaves, dried red chillies and the remaining 1/2 tsp whole panch phoron. Let them crackle 15 seconds.
steps.tip: The fenugreek in panch phoron turns bitter if it darkens past golden brown.

steps.text: Add the asafoetida and the grated ginger and stir for 30 seconds.
Tip in the potato and sweet potato and fry 4 minutes until the edges are translucent.
Add the pumpkin, raw banana, beans and cabbage with the turmeric, cumin powder and salt. Fold gently for 3 minutes.
Add the eggplant last, along with 200ml water. Cover and cook on low for 18-20 minutes.
steps.tip: Do not stir while it steams. Shake the pan by the handle instead.

steps.text: Uncover: the pumpkin should have collapsed and be binding everything into a rough mash.
steps.tip: That collapsing pumpkin is the texture you are after — if it still holds cubes, give it 5 more minutes covered.

steps.text: Cook uncovered 4-5 minutes to drive off the last of the water.
Stir in the sugar, garam masala and the crushed toasted panch phoron. Rest 5 minutes and serve with khichuri or rice.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and tastes better on day two. Reheat in a pan with a splash of water; it does not freeze well.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
